question: How is CLIP related to self-supervised contrastive learning?
direct_answer: CLIP uses a contrastive objective, but its pairs are image-text matches rather than two views of the same image.
expanded_answer: CLIP aligns embeddings from two modalities. Matched image-text pairs are pulled together and mismatched pairs are pushed apart. This is conceptually similar to contrastive self-supervision because it learns shared representations without manual class labels, but the supervision comes from naturally paired multimodal data instead of augmentation of a single example.
key_points: Learns general-purpose embeddings from paired data
common_wrong_ideas: CLIP is fully supervised in the usual label sense
CLIP does not use contrastive learning
Self-supervision can only use single-modality data
